clue.text: Deceptive appearance of work at the foot of the Pennines

definitions.text: at the foot of the Pennines
definitions.note: describes a place, the Derbyshire town standing below the hills

parts.note: a gloss is a superficial shine that hides what lies beneath
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone is fooled by how a job looks at the edge of England's northern hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names a location rather than a thing: GLOSSOP is a market town in Derbyshire, at the edge of the Pennines, the hill range running down northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derbyshire market town lies where the moors of the northern English hill chain begin.

clue.text: Manna from heaven?

parts.note: the food the Israelites received in the wilderness, read as any welcome gift

explanation.definitionFit: An unexpected blessing arriving just when needed, as if sent by the deity.

clue.text: Superior level of attainment reached in the aircraft industry, say

definitions.text: Superior level of attainment reached in the aircraft industry, say

parts.words: Superior level of attainment reached in the aircraft industry, say
parts.note: plane read as an aircraft as well as a level of thought, so better aeroplanes give a loftier level

explanation.surface: Aviation firms reach a higher standard.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at a more elevated intellectual or spiritual level.

clue.text: Fired at Q.C. providing material .

parts.note: fired as a gun is, shot
a Queen's Counsel, senior barrister, is said to take silk

explanation.surface: A lawyer comes under fire for supplying fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: A Queen's Counsel wears a silk gown, so 'silk' means a QC. The clue ends with an ellipsis that leads into 4 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabric woven with warp and weft of different colours so that it changes hue in the light.

clue.text: … for a crime put through to twelve good men and true

parts.note: per means for, as in so much per head
the traditional description of a jury

explanation.surface: An offence goes to trial before the jurors.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 3 down; 'put through to' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying under oath is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Hurriedly left without having eaten

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for having eaten wraps around the letter

parts.note: having eaten means fed

explanation.surface: Someone dashes off before their meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue both defines the answer and builds it: 'without' means outside, so FED goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away in haste, which is what someone did who hurriedly departed.

clue.text: Barrier for a sporting activity

explanation.surface: A fence put up for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence or row of fences forms a boundary; swordplay with foils is an Olympic sport.

clue.text: English painter in pretty good form

indicators.note: in shows the name sits inside the next word

explanation.surface: A British artist on fine form.
explanation.walkthrough: William Etty was a nineteenth-century English painter of nudes; 'good form' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty of York was a Victorian artist known for figure painting.

clue.text: No fat about the ironclad son of Banquo

indicators.note: clad means clothed, so the symbol for iron is wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
with no fat means lean
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A thin man in armour turns out to be a Shakespeare character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ironclad' is one printed word doing the work of two: its first half is the metal and its second half, 'clad', is the wrapping indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: In Macbeth, the boy who escapes when his father is murdered.

clue.text: One of a group getting up at 1745?

definitions.text: One of a group getting up at 1745?

parts.words: One of a group getting up at 1745?
parts.note: 1745 read as a year, not a time of day, and getting up as rebelling, not rising from bed

explanation.definitionFit: The 1745 Stuart rebellion in Scotland; one taking part was rebelling in it.

clue.text: Bellow for a living — and succeed?

explanation.surface: A town crier's career is a success.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition takes the idiom literally, a trade made of roaring; the dash then gives its real meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, someone whose job is bellowing has a trade of roars; as an idiom, the phrase means to prosper, doing brisk business.

clue.text: Improve on the ebb-tide

indicators.note: an ebbing tide flows back out, so the word tide is read backwards

parts.note: the second half of the compound ebb-tide, used whole; that it sits inside ebb-tide is a coincidence of the hyphenated phrase, not a hiding device

explanation.surface: Making something better as the sea recedes.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise a text is to correct and improve it.

clue.text: Collector's item in " Twelfth Night"

explanation.surface: Something a collector would prize turns up in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: Curio is one of Duke Orsino's attendants in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare object prized by a collector; and the name of a gentleman attending Duke Orsino in Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: Enlist a novel little woman in the end

parts.note: Jo March is one of the sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women

explanation.surface: A woman from a book signs up at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end' only says that IN comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up as a member, for example of the armed forces.

clue.text: The goodwill, it appears, in Miss Robsart

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the lady's first name

parts.note: Amy Robsart, wife of Robert Dudley, is the heroine of Walter Scott's Kenilworth
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tudor lady seems to show kindly feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Amy Robsart was the first wife of Robert Dudley, Elizabeth I's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly relations and good feeling between people or nations.

clue.text: Goes in with 12 to find the architect

indicators.note: the letters are put together afresh to discover the person named

parts.note: refers to the answer to 12 across, a word meaning enlist

explanation.surface: Someone enters alongside another to look for a building designer.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of GOES IN together with JOIN (the answer to 12) to get the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventeenth-century Englishman who designed the Banqueting House in Whitehall and brought Palladian style to Britain.

clue.text: Call me within twenty-four "hours here

indicators.note: within puts the call and the pronoun inside the period of time

parts.note: a day lasts twenty-four hours
ho is a call to attract attention
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be phoned at any hour in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' is the definition: DAHOMEY is the former name of Benin, in West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The West African kingdom, later a French colony, now known as Benin, is the place the clue points to.

clue.text: The range of heavy artillery

parts.note: range read as the place where big guns are set up, not how far they fire

explanation.surface: How far big guns can shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun emplacement is a position where heavy weapons are set out.

clue.text: Fitful crier at fault

indicators.note: at fault suggests these letters are wrong as they stand and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A town crier who is to blame proves unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fitful comes in irregular bursts, unpredictable and unsteady.

clue.text: Followed Rex in and made certain

indicators.note: in puts the king's letter inside the word for followed

parts.note: ensued means followed on
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: The king came after and made sure.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to guarantee that something happens.

clue.text: Surfaces at harvest-time

explanation.surface: Something emerges when the fields are reaped.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear unexpectedly; and, literally, the season when grain is gathered.

clue.text: Swell example of conceit at the top

parts.note: to swell is to grow larger, so swell suggests big
the head is the top of the body or of a list

explanation.surface: A grand show of vanity at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A boastful person is a living instance of vanity.

clue.text: Dim-sighted mad king in bed

indicators.note: in puts the monarch inside the sleeping place

parts.note: taken as written
King Lear goes mad in Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A deranged monarch lies in bed with poor eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are watery and unfocused, so vision is blurred.

clue.text: Granted it may be used by the law to track down wanted persons

definitions.text: Granted it may be used by the law to track down wanted persons

indicators.note: the letters of the first word are used in another order

explanation.surface: Admittedly, the police could deploy it to catch fugitives.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole the clue both builds and defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A police net is a systematic sweep to catch suspects.

clue.text: See 3
See 14
Is turned against a Hindu. deity

indicators.note: turned means the word is is read the other way round

parts.note: v, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: Someone turns against a god of India.
explanation.walkthrough: The stop after 'Hindu' is a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiva, also spelt this way, is the destroyer god of the Hindu trinity.

clue.text: Region centrally placed in Near East

indicators.note: taking the central letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A zone in the middle of the Levant.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone or district of land.

clue.text: Old French coin about right for the material

indicators.note: about means the coin goes around the letter

parts.note: the ecu was an old French coin

explanation.surface: An antique coin is about the right price for fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbleached linen fabric, or its beige colour.

clue.text: It's bound to prevent overcharging for letters

definitions.text: It's bound to prevent overcharging for letters

parts.words: It's bound to prevent overcharging for letters
parts.note: letters read as people who let property, landlords, not alphabet characters, and bound as a legal limit

explanation.surface: A rule that stops the post office charging too much on mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal cap on what landlords may demand from tenants.

clue.text: Improvise with a 5-amp fuse

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
taken as written

explanation.surface: Making do with a small electrical fuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To vamp is to play a made-up accompaniment, extemporising music.

clue.text: Once felt it might be put under the carpet

definitions.text: Once felt it might be put under the carpet

parts.words: Once felt it might be put under the carpet
parts.note: felt read as the fabric, not the past of feel: a coarse cloth used long ago as a floor covering

explanation.surface: Someone used to think a matter could be hushed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse woollen fabric laid on floors, often beneath or over a rug.
